rules.title: Jersey City ban on algorithmic rent-setting software (e.g., RealPage)
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, including revenue management software that relies on nonpublic competitor data, to set rents.
rules.key_value: $2,000 daily fine (as described in public comment)
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential landlords in Jersey City using rent-setting algorithms or revenue management software; per the article, the measure targets use of nonpublic data and coordination among landlords.
rules.exemptions: According to the article, real estate agents were excluded at the request of the NJ Association of Realtors. A further exclusion for Multiple Listing Services was requested, but the article does not say it was adopted. A speaker referred to owners of multiple buildings using algorithms without colluding as excluded.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Whether the landlord uses software relying on nonpublic competitor data; the exact scope of the exclusions is not stated.

rules.penalty: A $2,000 daily fine, as referenced by a public commenter.
rules.citation: Jersey City ordinance sponsored by Councilman James Solomon (ordinance number not given in source)
rules.quoted_span: The Jersey City Council unanimously approved (9-0) a measure banning rent-setting algorithms such as RealPage, as well as increasing benefits for laborers, at last night’s meeting.
rules.conflict_note: This is a news article and gives no ordinance number, publication date, passage date, or effective date. Status is inferred as in force on the assumption that the council's passage was final adoption. Council members raised enforceability concerns and said amendments may still happen. The House of Representatives was reported to be considering federal preemption of such municipal bans. The $2,000 daily fine comes only from a public commenter's remarks.
